July 9, 1932
Executive Order
FURTHER TEMPORARY EXEMPTION OF CERTAIN PERSONS FROM COMPUL-
SORY RETIREMENT FOR AGE IN ORDER TO AFFORD
TIME FOR FILLING VACANCIES
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204 of Part II of the act
entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933, and for other purposes ," approved
June 30 , 1932, the following-named persons who have reached the retirement age
prescribed for automatic separation from the service and who were temporarily
exempted from the provisions of that section and continued in the service until July
10 , 1932, by Executive order dated June 30 , 1932 (No. 5874), are hereby further
temporarily exempted from the provisions of that section and continued in the service
until August 1, 1932 :
Name
William L.

research_rationale:
EO 5881 (July 9, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 further exempting William L. Hill, John Lewis May and Leonard Magruder (Treasury) from compulsory retirement 'and continued in the service until August 1, 1932', to afford time to appoint successors. It follows EO 5874 (June 30, 1932), whose exemption ran to July 10, 1932. The order ends by its own terms on 1932-08-01. NOTE: the machine TERM record's stated_end_date (1932-07-10) misreads the recital of EO 5874's earlier term; its span (chars 910-1759 of the held text) contains the operative words 'until August 1, 1932', which govern. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.

The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act. The recited July 10, 1932 date is the end of the earlier exemption under EO 5874, not of this order; this order's own term starts where that one stopped. Executive Order 5982. December 22, 1932
Executive Order
EXEMPTION OF CHARLES J. HARLOW FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FOR AGE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204 of Part II of the act
entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , and for other purposes ," approved June
30 , 1932, Charles J. Harlow, plate printer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the
Department of Commerce , who, during the current month , reaches the retirement
age prescribed for automatic separation from the service , is hereby exempted from the
provisions of that section until March 31 , 1933 .

research_rationale:
EO 5982 (Dec. 22, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), exempts Charles J. Harlow, plate printer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey, from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 'until March 31, 1933'. Single time-limited grant ending by its own terms on 1933-03-31. The held OCR text omits the signature line; the compilation page, not the OCR, is the original, and the operative text is complete. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms expiry on the stated date. An individual employee's death or voluntary separation before that date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, a termination of the order; no held record shows any such event, and no later order amends, revokes or extends this order before the stated date (see search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act. Searches judged adequate for this narrow, short-lived exemption: the USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude any current-law reference, and the OFR catalog search (1937 onward, coverage warning) is supplemented by my own bounded search, on 2026-10-19, of the held WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, every numbered entry) and of all 526 held Hoover OFR 1974 compilation texts (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts) for each exempted person's surname. That search found the serial extension orders that do exist for other persons in this family (EO 6615 and EO 6974 for Jacob L. Nuber, EO 6975 for Charles J. James) but no later order naming the person(s) exempted by this order.","independent_command_check":"The order contains a single operative command (the time-limited exemption); the recital of authority and the identification of the employee(s) are not independent commands.
